guides.title: MacBook Pro 14" Battery Replacement
guides.introduction: This guide walks you through replacing the battery in your MacBook Pro 14" (2023). The battery is secured with strong adhesive strips. Take your time and work slowly.
guides.conclusion: Reassemble in reverse order. Calibrate the new battery by charging to 100%, then running it down to 10%, then charging uninterrupted to 100%.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Power Down & Remove Bottom Case
steps.instruction: Shut down your MacBook completely. Close the lid and flip it over. Remove all eight P5 Pentalobe screws around the perimeter of the bottom case. The screws near the hinge are slightly longer — note their positions. Use a suction handle to gently lift the bottom case starting from the front edge.
warnings: Ensure the MacBook is fully powered off, not just sleeping.
tips: Keep screws organized — the two near the hinge are longer.
The bottom case is held by clips in addition to screws.

steps.title: Disconnect the Battery
steps.instruction: Locate the battery connector on the logic board. It's a small white plug near the center of the board. Use a plastic spudger to gently pry the connector straight up from its socket. Do NOT pull on the wires. This disconnects power to the entire system for safe repair.
warnings: ALWAYS disconnect the battery before touching any other component.
Never use metal tools near the battery connector.
tips: The connector pops straight up — don't slide it sideways.

steps.title: Remove Battery Adhesive Strips
steps.instruction: The battery is held down by six stretch-release adhesive strips. Find the black pull tabs at the edges of the battery. Pull each tab slowly at a LOW angle (almost parallel to the battery surface). If a strip breaks, apply a small amount of adhesive remover and wait 2 minutes before prying.
warnings: Do NOT bend or puncture the battery — it can catch fire.
If a strip breaks, don't force the battery. Use adhesive remover.
tips: Pull slowly and steadily. Speed is your enemy here.
Heat the bottom of the case with a hair dryer for 30 seconds to soften adhesive.

steps.title: Lift Out the Battery
steps.instruction: Once all adhesive strips are released, gently lift the battery from the side nearest the trackpad. It should come free easily. If it resists, check for remaining adhesive. Place the old battery in a safe container.
warnings: Do not reuse old adhesive strips.
tips: Note the battery orientation for installing the new one.

steps.title: Install New Battery
steps.instruction: Peel the protective film from the new battery's adhesive strips. Carefully align the battery in the same position as the original. Press firmly for 30 seconds to set the adhesive. Reconnect the battery cable by pressing it straight down into the socket until it clicks.
warnings: Ensure the connector is fully seated — partial connection can cause boot issues.
tips: Test the MacBook before replacing the bottom case.

steps.title: Reassemble & Test
steps.instruction: Replace the bottom case, starting with the hinge-side clips. Press down around the edges until all clips engage. Reinsert the eight Pentalobe screws — the longer ones near the hinge. Power on and verify the battery is recognized in System Settings > Battery.
warnings: Do not overtighten the Pentalobe screws — they strip easily.
tips: If the MacBook doesn't power on, recheck the battery connector.

guides.title: MacBook Pro 14" SSD Upgrade
guides.introduction: Note: SSD upgrades on M2 Pro/Max MacBook Pro models are limited. This guide covers SSD removal for data recovery or replacement with an identical Apple SSD module.
guides.conclusion: If replacing with a new SSD, you'll need to reinstall macOS via Internet Recovery (Cmd+Option+R at boot).
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Case
steps.instruction: Power off the MacBook. Remove all eight P5 Pentalobe screws and lift off the bottom case.
warnings: Ensure MacBook is fully powered off.

steps.title: Disconnect Battery
steps.instruction: Use a spudger to disconnect the battery connector from the logic board for safety.
warnings: Always disconnect battery before working on components.

steps.title: Remove SSD Mounting Screw
steps.instruction: Locate the SSD module near the top-left of the logic board. Remove the single T5 Torx retaining screw.
tips: The screw is captive — it won't come all the way out.

steps.title: Remove SSD Module
steps.instruction: Gently pull the SSD straight out of its connector. Pull evenly — don't rock it side to side. Place it in an anti-static bag.
warnings: Handle by the edges only. Do not touch the gold connectors.
tips: If the SSD is stuck, use a spudger to gently lever it from the end.

steps.title: Install New SSD & Reassemble
steps.instruction: Insert the replacement SSD into the connector at the same angle. Press it flat and secure with the T5 Torx screw. Reconnect the battery, replace the bottom case, and boot into Internet Recovery to install macOS.
tips: Hold Cmd+Option+R at boot for Internet Recovery.

guides.title: Dell XPS 15 Battery Replacement
guides.introduction: The Dell XPS 15 battery is one of the easiest to replace among premium laptops. No adhesive — just screws and a cable.
guides.conclusion: Dispose of the old battery at a certified electronics recycling center. Never throw lithium-ion batteries in the trash.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Panel
steps.instruction: Power off the XPS 15 and close the lid. Remove all 10 T5 Torx screws from the bottom panel. Two screws near the hinge are captive and won't come out completely. Use a plastic pry tool along the front edge to release the clips, then lift the panel from the hinge end.
warnings: Be gentle with the clips — they can break if forced.
tips: Start prying from the front center and work outward.

steps.title: Disconnect Battery Cable
steps.instruction: Locate the battery cable connector on the motherboard (near the center). Use a spudger to gently pry it straight up. This cuts power to the system for safe work.
warnings: Always disconnect battery first before touching anything else.

steps.title: Remove Battery Screws
steps.instruction: Remove the 6 Phillips #0 screws securing the battery to the chassis. Note their positions — some may be different lengths.
tips: Use a magnetic mat to organize screws.

steps.title: Remove Battery
steps.instruction: The battery may have pull-tab adhesive. Pull the tabs at a low angle. If they break, gently pry the battery with a plastic spudger. Lift the battery out.
warnings: Do not bend or puncture the battery.
tips: The XPS battery is usually not heavily glued — it should come out easily.

steps.title: Install New Battery & Reassemble
steps.instruction: Place the new battery in position and secure with the 6 Phillips screws. Reconnect the battery cable. Replace the bottom panel, starting clips from the hinge end, then reinstall all 10 Torx screws.
tips: Power on before replacing the bottom panel to verify the battery is detected.

guides.title: Dell XPS 15 RAM Upgrade
guides.introduction: Upgrading RAM on the Dell XPS 15 is straightforward — the SO-DIMM slots are immediately accessible after removing the bottom panel.
guides.conclusion: The XPS 15 supports up to 64GB DDR5 (2x32GB). Match speeds for best performance.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Panel
steps.instruction: Remove all 10 T5 Torx screws and pry off the bottom panel starting from the front edge.

steps.title: Disconnect Battery
steps.instruction: Disconnect the battery cable from the motherboard for safety.
warnings: Always disconnect power before handling RAM.

steps.title: Remove Existing RAM
steps.instruction: Locate the SO-DIMM slots (gold-edged modules). Push the metal retention clips on both sides outward — the module will pop up at a 30° angle. Pull the module straight out. Repeat for the second slot if present.
warnings: Handle RAM by the edges only. Do not touch gold contacts.
tips: Note the notch orientation — RAM only fits one way.

steps.title: Install New RAM
steps.instruction: Insert the new SO-DIMM module at a 30° angle, aligning the notch with the slot key. Press firmly until the retention clips snap into place on both sides. Repeat for the second module if installing two.
warnings: Use matched pairs for dual-channel performance.
tips: DDR5 modules have a different notch position than DDR4 — they are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Reconnect Battery & Reassemble
steps.instruction: Reconnect the battery cable. Replace the bottom panel and all 10 screws. Power on and check System Information to verify the new RAM is detected.
tips: First boot after RAM change may take 30-60 seconds while the system trains memory.

guides.title: ThinkPad X1 Carbon SSD Upgrade
guides.introduction: The ThinkPad X1 Carbon has an easily accessible M.2 SSD slot. This is one of the simplest upgrades you can perform.
guides.conclusion: After installing the new SSD, boot from a USB installer or use Lenovo's recovery media to install your OS.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Cover
steps.instruction: Power off the ThinkPad. Flip it over and loosen the 5 captive Phillips screws. They stay attached to the cover. Use a plastic spudger along the front edge to release clips, then lift the cover off.
tips: The captive screws are convenient — you can't lose them!

steps.title: Locate & Remove SSD Screw
steps.instruction: Find the M.2 SSD — a small rectangular card near the center of the board. Remove the single Phillips screw holding it in place.
tips: The screw is small — use a magnetized screwdriver to avoid losing it.

steps.title: Remove Old SSD
steps.instruction: Gently pull the SSD straight out of the M.2 connector at a slight upward angle. Store it in an anti-static bag if you plan to keep it.
warnings: Do not force it — it should slide out smoothly.

steps.title: Install New SSD
steps.instruction: Insert the new M.2 SSD into the connector at a slight angle (about 15°). Press it down flat and secure with the Phillips screw. Replace the bottom cover and power on.
tips: Use PCIe Gen 4 NVMe SSDs for best performance in this machine.

guides.title: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Battery Replacement
guides.introduction: Replacing the battery in the X1 Carbon requires removing the bottom cover and disconnecting a single cable. Straightforward but requires care around the battery cells.
guides.conclusion: Lenovo batteries can be ordered directly from Lenovo parts or authorized resellers. Verify the FRU number matches your model.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Cover
steps.instruction: Power off the ThinkPad. Loosen the 5 captive Phillips screws and remove the bottom cover.

steps.title: Disconnect Battery Cable
steps.instruction: Locate the battery cable (white connector near the battery edge). Use a spudger to pry it straight up from the system board.
warnings: Disconnecting the battery prevents short circuits during repair.

steps.title: Remove Battery Screws
steps.instruction: Remove the 4 Phillips screws securing the battery to the chassis.

steps.title: Lift Out Battery
steps.instruction: Gently lift the battery out. It may have light adhesive — use a spudger if needed. Do not bend or puncture the cells.
warnings: Never puncture or bend lithium-ion battery cells.

steps.title: Install New Battery
steps.instruction: Place the new battery in position. Secure with 4 Phillips screws. Reconnect the battery cable. Replace the bottom cover and test.
tips: Check Lenovo Vantage for battery health after replacement.

guides.title: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Keyboard Replacement
guides.introduction: The X1 Carbon keyboard replacement is more involved than on older ThinkPads. The palmrest must be removed to access the keyboard from underneath.
guides.conclusion: Test all keys thoroughly before final reassembly. Use Lenovo's keyboard test utility or an online key tester.
guides.author: RepairAR Team

steps.title: Remove Bottom Cover & Battery
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom cover (5 captive screws) and disconnect/remove the battery for safety.

steps.title: Disconnect Keyboard Cable
steps.instruction: From the bottom of the laptop, locate the keyboard ribbon cable connected to the system board. Flip up the locking flap and gently pull the cable out.
warnings: The locking flap is fragile — lift gently.

steps.title: Release Keyboard Tabs
steps.instruction: On the bottom of the chassis, there are small access holes. Use a spudger to push through each hole to release the keyboard retention tabs. There are typically 5-6 tabs along the top edge.
warnings: Push gently — the tabs can break if forced.
tips: Work from the center outward.

steps.title: Remove Old Keyboard
steps.instruction: Flip the laptop right-side up. Open the lid. The keyboard should now lift out from the top. If it resists, check for remaining tabs. Tilt it up and slide the ribbon cable out through the slot.
tips: Note how the ribbon cable routes through the slot.

steps.title: Install New Keyboard
steps.instruction: Thread the new keyboard's ribbon cable through the slot. Align the keyboard with the retention slots and press down until all tabs click into place. Reconnect the cable from the bottom, replace the battery, and close up.
warnings: Ensure the ribbon cable is fully seated before locking.
tips: Test all keys before replacing the bottom cover.
